title: Act II, Scene I

teacherSummary.text: After midnight Banquo, unable to sleep, tells Fleance of 'cursed thoughts' and gives Macbeth a diamond from the king for Lady Macbeth. Banquo mentions dreaming of the Witches; Macbeth claims he does not think of them and hints at future honor if Banquo will 'cleave to my consent'; Banquo agrees only if he keeps his allegiance clear. Alone, Macbeth sees a dagger in the air leading him to Duncan, wonders if it is 'a dagger of the mind', and goes when the bell rings: 'Hear it not, Duncan; for it is a knell.'

context.history: Plays at the Globe were performed in daylight, so night had to be created by words: references to darkness, torches and the bell signal the hour.

significance: The dagger soliloquy dramatizes a mind dividing against itself; whether the dagger is supernatural or hallucinated is left open, a pattern the play repeats with Banquo's ghost.
discussionQuestions: Have you ever been so anxious or guilty that you imagined something that was not there?

middleSchool.note: Excerpt-based: read the passage aloud first; use the scaffolds; accept partial answers and build with probes.

hsFreshman.note: Use the scaffolds for literal and inferential items; require one quotation for every inferential answer.

hsSophomore.note: Require a quotation and an explanation; push evaluative answers to address a counterclaim.

hsJunior.note: Emphasize structure and ambiguity; students should name where the text leaves matters open.

hsSenior.note: Weigh competing interpretations; students should defend the stronger reading.
